title: a-chart-tree-tooth-asserts-a-refusal-the-orient-door-never-reaches
author: CC
owner: CC builds it; cairn/tools/tree owns the tooth
intention: cairn/tools/tree/proofs/test_chart_tree.py::test_gate_before_seed is RED and has been for at least one commit. It fires deposit_orient with a berth_path that does not exist and asserts the refusal says 'does not exist'. The orient door refuses EARLIER, on provenance — the fixture _packet() (test_chart_tree.py:70-93) declares only {"intent": "cc", "scope": "cc"}, so the door answers 'provenance does not cover: domain, refs, unknowns' and the berth-existence check is never reached. Fix the tooth so it measures the thing it names: give the fixture a provenance the door accepts, so the only remaining lack is the missing berth.
why: Law 9 — a red is a red and carries no triage authority; and Law 8 — a tooth that asserts a refusal the code never reaches is proving the door's FIRST check twice and its named check not at all. The tooth reads as coverage of berth-existence and covers nothing of the kind, which is the hollow shape the whole proof corpus exists against.
how: Widen the fixture's provenance in _packet() to cover domain, refs and unknowns (the door's own required set — read it off the refusal text rather than guessing), leaving berth_path pointing at a path that does not exist. Then assert BOTH: that the message names the missing berth, and — as the control that keeps this from re-rotting — that a packet with the SAME provenance and an existing berth is accepted. Do not relax the door.
falsifier: DONE when test_gate_before_seed fails for the reason it names: with the fixture's provenance accepted, the refusal text carries 'does not exist' and names the berth path, and the same packet with a real berth passes. WRONG INTENT if the tooth is made green by loosening the orient door's provenance requirement, or by asserting on whichever refusal happens to come back first — either would trade a visible red for an invisible hollow.
traces_to: Law 9 (red is the default; green is earned — and a standing red is not a resting state); Law 8 (nothing enters proven-space without a proof a hollow build couldn't pass); Law 3 (the tooth's claim about what it measures was unmeasured until it was run).
watchme: none, because the fix is a single tooth in a single file and its own green-and-control pair IS the standing check; a probe watching one assertion would be a second copy of that assertion.
gates_bound: proof gate — cairn/tools/tree/proofs/test_chart_tree.py runs green under the tester at isolation=netns, and the repaired tooth reds against the un-repaired fixture.
feeds back to origin on failure — a red routes to this ticket's own voyage, never to a paragraph.
durability gate — not done until proven AND committed.
children: none, because it is one tooth in one file

decisions.text: In cairn/tools/tree/proofs/test_chart_tree.py, _packet()'s provenance becomes {'intent':'cc','scope':'cc','domain':'cc','refs':'cc','unknowns':'cc'} — stratum 'cc' for all five (it is in orient's _STRATA_ACCEPTED and matches the two keys already there). The fixture stands for a BERTHED packet: the write door stamps domain/refs/unknowns, the deposit door measures nothing and only requires coverage, so with all five covered deposit_orient reaches its berth-existence check.
decisions.step: unlisted: widen _packet() provenance to cover domain, refs, and unknowns

decisions.text: test_gate_before_seed keeps its FIRST refusal exactly as it stands (the malformed packet: _refuses(OrientRefused, deposit_orient, {'intent':'x'}, ...) — leave that call untouched). Its SECOND call passes _packet() with berth_path=os.path.join(tmp,'no-such-berth.json') and asserts three things on the message: 'does not exist' in msg, the missing path in msg, and 'provenance does not cover' NOT in msg (that would mean the refusal came one lack early). Then assert trees.tree_state(_NEXUS, table=_TABLE, owner='chart') == before. THE CONTROL, last: control = _packet(intent='the gate control packet of the chart tree proof [' + _NEXUS + ']'); berth = _berthed_fixture(tmp, control); r = deposit_orient(control, [1.0,0.0,0.0], berth_path=berth, nexus=_NEXUS); _CREATED_NODES.append(r['node_id']) (the proof's existing teardown deletes every id in that list); assert r['duplicate'] is False. decisions.text: test_gate_before_seed's mechanics, as built at cairn/tools/tree/proofs/test_chart_tree.py: (a) before = trees.tree_state(_NEXUS, table=_TABLE, owner='chart') is captured as the tooth's FIRST line, before any deposit_orient call, and the tree-unchanged assertion compares against it after both refusals and before the control; (b) _packet(...) (line 77) is the fixture function whose every provenance field is a keyword argument with a default — _packet() yields a berthed-shaped packet, _packet(intent='...') overrides one field; (c) both refusals go through _refuses(exc, fn, *args, **kwargs) (line 69), which calls fn, asserts exc was raised, and returns str(exc) — the missing-berth call is msg = _refuses(OrientRefused, deposit_orient, _packet(), [1.0, 0.0, 0.0], berth_path=<no-such-berth path>) and the three assertions ('does not exist', the berth path, not 'provenance does not cover') read msg.

_packet() as built (cairn/tools/tree/proofs/test_chart_tree.py lines 77-106) is a plain function: def _packet(intent='wire the tree stratum into the orient nexus of the chart device', **over) builds the dict p = {'intent': intent, 'domain': 'chart — the nexus machinery', 'scope': 'IN: the orient nexus's tree. OUT: everything else.', 'refs': ['tree'], 'unknowns': [], 'confidence': 0.7, 'provenance': {'intent': 'cc', 'scope': 'cc', 'domain': 'cc', 'refs': 'cc', 'unknowns': 'cc'}}, then p.update(over) and returns p. The widening was adding the three keys domain/refs/unknowns = 'cc' to that provenance dict; nothing else in the fixture moved.

Everything test_gate_before_seed depends on is module-scope in test_chart_tree.py, no pytest: os, json, tempfile, datetime, Path imported at lines 34-40; trees is cairn.devices.librarian.trees (line 56); OrientRefused and deposit_orient from cairn.devices.codemother.machines.orient.orient (line 50); _NEXUS (line 64, an orient_<pid>_<hhmmss> nexus name) and _TABLE = nexus_table(_NEXUS) (line 65); _refuses(exc, fn, *args, **kwargs) at line 69; _packet(intent=..., **over) at line 77; _berthed_fixture(tmp, packet) at line 109 writes packet as JSON to <tmp>/orient-20260728T120000-feedfacecafe.json and returns that path; tmp is a tempfile.TemporaryDirectory() opened inside the tooth (line 139), not a fixture; _CREATED_NODES is the module-level list the teardown reads to delete every node a tooth registered.

The orient door's berth-existence refusal is fixed text at cairn/devices/codemother/machines/orient/orient.py line 543-546: deposit_orient first runs validate_orient(packet, root=root, measure_provenance=False) (which is where 'provenance does not cover: ...' comes from, and which a D1-shaped packet passes), then, when berth_path is not a str or os.path.isfile(os.path.expanduser(berth_path)) is False, raises OrientRefused(f"deposit_orient: berth {berth_path!r} does not exist on disk — a node whose provenance points at nothing is fabricated attribution one layer up; nothing landed"). So the message carries the literal 'does not exist' and the berth path (repr-quoted), and never 'provenance does not cover'.
